Moved a heavy package on the hand truck
Anything 50 lb or more goes on the hand truck (or gets a second person). Don't carry what you can wheel.
Climbed down from the cab with three points of contact
Use three points of contact getting in and out of the truck. Jumping down is one of the most common ways couriers get hurt.
Climbed back into the cab safely
Grab handle, one step at a time, and never jump up while carrying anything.
Clear trip hazards off the walkway with E, even with a package in hand: set it down, move them, pick it up.
Slow down on ice, wet steps and cluttered walkways. Short steps, eyes on the path, a hand free for balance.
Hold SHIFT and take short steps over anything slippery or cluttered, above all with a package that hides your feet.
Slow down BEFORE the slippery patch: hold SHIFT for short steps from the first one.
Slow down and step carefully (hold SHIFT) over uneven ground.
Match the label address against the stop before delivering. Scanning catches wrong-stop packages.
Misdelivery: another customer's package left here
Delivered every piece for this stop
Check the piece count ("1 of 2") and pull every piece for the stop.
Scanned the package before leaving the truck
Scan before you step out. It confirms the stop and shows signature needs before you walk to the door.
Every stop needs a record: a delivery with proof, or an exception code.
Chose the right way to deliver

Delivered when the rules said not to

Signature-required package handed to a person
Never leave a signature-required package unattended. Get a signature or record an exception and leave a door tag.
Follow the customer's delivery note when it's safe to.
A POD photo shows the package and where it was left (the door or doorstep). Never a house number, and never people or any part of one, yours included.
Knocked or rang before leaving the package
Recorded the signer's real printed name
Record the printed name of whoever actually signed, even if that isn't the addressee.
Left a door tag for the customer
When a delivery attempt fails, leave a door tag so the customer knows what happened and what to do next.
Kept the package secure on the truck
After an exception the package goes back on the truck. Never leave it behind.
Made a real attempt before the exception
Knock or ring and wait a moment before recording that nobody was available.
In the heat, drink water before you feel thirsty: a few sips at every stop, even if you don't feel like it.
Kept body heat out of the danger zone
Use shade and the truck's AC to cool down between stops, and slow your pace in extreme heat.
Checked the photo ID properly (age, expiry, name)
Adult signature means a valid, unexpired photo ID showing the person is 21 or older. Check the date of birth against today's date.
Checked the house number against the label
Check the number on the building against the label. "Close enough" addresses cause misdeliveries.
Plan the stop before you step out: package pulled, scanned and ready. It saves walks back to the truck.
Pulled only the right package from the shelves
Read the whole address (number, street and unit) before pulling a package. Near-matches are easy to grab.
